name: Ratboys
label: New West
lede: Julia Steiner and Dave Sagan met in a Notre Dame Facebook group in 2010, went through nine drummers on the way to a four-piece, and in 2026 made a record about talking to an empty chair.

eras.title: A Facebook group and a swimming pool
eras.text: Steiner and Sagan write acoustic songs in dorms, basements and a converted school pool in South Bend. A class assignment in 2014 nudges them toward electric guitars.

years.src: Notre Dame Magazine · Human Pursuits · Wikipedia: Ratboys
years.h: Steiner spots a bass in Sagan's profile photo
years.p: Julia Steiner liked a funny comment Dave Sagan left in the Notre Dame class-of-2014 Facebook group, saw him holding a bass in his profile picture and started messaging. They met on campus that fall.
years.xp:
Notre Dame Magazine tells it this way: Steiner saw the comment, saw the bass, and wrote to him. Their musical backgrounds differed, and the connection was immediate anyway.

Sagan grew up in Oak Forest, a south suburb of Chicago, and later pulled Steiner into the city's DIY scene. Wikipedia dates the band's formation to fall 2010.

years.src: Notre Dame Magazine · Treble · Wikipedia: Ratboys
years.h: Ratboy arrives on Swerp Records
years.p: Five lo-fi acoustic songs from a duo that hasn't plugged in yet.
years.xp:
The name was Steiner's high school nickname, from a lunch-table game where friends handed each other weird names. The plural came after another musician called Ratboy sent them a threatening email about it, per Notre Dame Magazine.

They played wherever South Bend let them: Acousticafe, the Riley Hall art building, a Breen-Phillips basement, the Reckers snack bar, the Mendoza business school courtyard. Steiner says they liked being a little rogue.

years.h: A South Bend apartment built in a school pool hosts the shows
years.p: From 2011 to 2015 The Pool gave Steiner her first DIY room, and the idea that the scene was for her too.
years.xp: Steiner told Notre Dame Magazine that The Pool made her feel comfortable and safe in a DIY environment, and empowered to go looking for that scene elsewhere.

years.h: A class on women in rock gets two songs recorded
years.p: Steiner wrote and recorded "Collected" and "Space Blows" for the class project, and they came out as singles in May 2014.
years.xp:
The assignment let students write a paper or make a creative project. Steiner chose two original songs about what women face in music, and the band says it pushed them toward louder, electric arrangements.

Both songs came back as re-recordings on Happy Birthday, Ratboy in 2021.

eras.title: Sagan graduates, and the van takes over
eras.text: Topshelf puts out a debut, the duo books itself across the country, and the rhythm section finally stops rotating.

years.h: Topshelf releases AOID, with the vocals cut at night
years.p: Recorded at the Owlery in Chicago in late 2014, with Steiner alone in the room for her vocal takes.
years.xp:
Mike Politowicz of Dowsing connected the band with Topshelf. Several songs, including "Charles Bernstein" and "Our Mortician's Daughter", had been live staples since mid-2012, and "Postman Song" dated to 2007.

The Chicago Tribune's Kevin Williams called it "almost like a sketch", really good but incomplete. GoldFlakePaint put it on its 2015 year-end list.

years.h: Sagan graduates, and the duo books 22 shows in 22 days
years.p: The run started in Kalamazoo, Michigan and ended in New Orleans, mostly in basements and bars.
years.xp:
Notre Dame Magazine quotes the plan as 22 basements and bars in 22 days. The band has funded itself with gig work such as DoorDash and Instacart.

Wikipedia adds that they toured the US and Europe with Pinegrove, Sorority Noise, Free Throw and Dowsing, and put out a 2016 split with Dowsing.

years.h: After nine drummers, Marcus Nuccio stays
years.p: Sean Neumann had joined on bass in 2016. Nuccio, who also plays in Pet Symmetry, took the drum seat in 2017, per Paste.
years.xp: Steiner told Treble that a booking agent approached them at a New York show where they were opening for Nuccio's other band, Pet Symmetry: "The fact that anyone wanted to invest their time with working with us was a big turning point for us." Neumann and Sagan both grew up in Chicago's southern suburbs.

years.cap: Ratboys opening for PUP at Bogart's, Cincinnati
yt: Elvis Is in the Freezer (official video)
years.h: Rolling Stone files GN under great albums you probably missed
years.p: Topshelf released it June 30, recorded at Atlas Studios with Mike Crotty; the list was 15 albums long.
years.xp:
Metacritic scores it 77. Steven Hyden picked it among 2017's best at Uproxx, and in 2025 ranked it 98th on his list of the best indie rock albums of the century, calling it "a foundational melding of emo and alt-country."

Wikipedia says the band toured two years behind it across the US, Canada, Europe and Japan, with Soccer Mommy, PUP, Diet Cig and Wild Pink.

eras.title: An empty house in Louisville
eras.text: Steiner writes alone in her childhood home, the four-piece cuts its first record together, and a pandemic cancels the victory lap.

years.cap: Ratboys at Lincoln Hall, Chicago, February 2020
years.src: Wikipedia: Printer's Devil (album) · Paste · Wikipedia: Ratboys
years.h: Steiner writes Printer's Devil in her empty childhood home
years.p: The house was in Louisville, Kentucky. The full four-piece then cut the record with Erik Rasmussen at Decade Music Studio in Chicago.
years.xp: It was the first record with the full four-piece, out February 28 on Topshelf. Paste says they had 10 days in the studio. Pitchfork scored it 7.7 and MTV called it the best album of their career. The lead single was "Alien with a Sleep Mask On".

years.h: SXSW cancels, and Ratboys move into a Discord
years.p: Three members were living together when COVID hit; a Patreon, a Discord and Twitch streams kept fans close.
years.xp: Paste reports the cancelled 2020 SXSW slot was meant to celebrate Printer's Devil. The band says the lockdown gave them time to work on new songs together, which shaped the next record.

eras.title: Seattle, on tape
eras.text: Ratboys re-record their first songs, meet Chris Walla on tour, sell camping trips for Walmart and open for the Decemberists.

years.h: Happy Birthday, Ratboy lands as a surprise on the EP's 10th birthday
years.p: All five songs from the original EP get the full-band treatment, along with five more early songs and "Go Outside".
years.xp: Stereogum describes it as an anniversary surprise with the current full lineup filling out the old duo songs. Pitchfork's Pete Tosiello gave it 7.2, saying it "contrasts cozy nostalgia with hard-rocking instincts."

years.h: Opening for Foxing in Montreal, they meet Chris Walla
years.p: Walla, the Death Cab for Cutie founder, had produced Tegan and Sara's The Con, which Steiner had just discovered.
years.xp: Paste reports Walla and the band met when they opened for Foxing in Montreal, then traded voice memos ahead of recording. The Window took 24 days at his Hall of Justice studio in Seattle, against the 10 days spent on Printer's Devil.

years.h: "Go Outside" sells Walmart camping trips
years.p: Walmart used the song in a camping spot in its "So Much More" campaign.
years.xp: Secret Road reports the placement; the band had no comment on that page. Nashville Scene later noted the commercial as a moment that widened their audience.

years.cap: Ratboys at Brighton Music Hall, Boston, Sept 28, 2023
years.src: Wikipedia: The Window (Ratboys album) · Paste · Treble
years.h: The Window goes to tape in Chris Walla's Seattle studio
years.p: Recorded in February 2022 at the Hall of Justice, the room Nirvana's Bleach and Sleater-Kinney's Dig Me Out came from.
years.xp:
Wikipedia says the title track grew out of Steiner's grandfather being unable to say goodbye to his hospitalized wife, seeing her only through a nursing home window. It was the first record where all four members shaped songs from the start, and it came out August 25.

Pitchfork scored it 8.0; it made Paste's year-end list at number 5, Stereogum's at 6 and Exclaim!'s at 8. The Chicago Tribune called it the band's most confident, assured version.

years.src: Nashville Scene · Notre Dame Magazine · Wikipedia: Singin' to an Empty Chair
years.h: Ratboys open for the Decemberists, then play 85 shows of their own
years.p: The Decemberists' 2024 tour gave them the big rooms; Notre Dame Magazine counts 85 shows for the year.
years.xp:
Notre Dame Magazine adds that they've played Lollapalooza. Nashville Scene reports headline dates that November, including a Blue Room set at Third Man Records in Nashville.

Decemberists keyboardist Jenny Conlee ended up playing Hammond organ on their next record.

eras.title: Singing to an empty chair
eras.text: They sign to New West, write in a Wisconsin cabin and track at Electrical Audio in Chicago. The album that comes out of it is about a fractured relationship, and the reviews are the strongest of their career.

years.src: Wikipedia: Singin' to an Empty Chair
years.h: A Wisconsin cabin, then Steve Albini's Electrical Audio
years.p: They wrote at Driftless Cabin in Richland Center, Wisconsin, then tracked with Walla at Electrical Audio in Chicago.
years.xp: Wikipedia says Walla stressed emotional impact over music theory and arrangement, and that at Electrical Audio they built a Doppler effect with a spinning turntable. Sessions also ran at Rosebud in Evanston.

years.cap: Ratboys at Mutations Festival, Brighton, UK, November 2025
years.h: After five albums on Topshelf, Ratboys sign to New West
years.p: "Light Night Mountains All That" arrives with a video Marcus Nuccio directed, and a North American tour is announced for February 2026.
years.xp: Steiner told Exclaim! her original idea was an ultra-high energy folk song in the style of the Dodos' Visiter, with spooky, pastoral imagery, and that it turned into a rural vision-quest during a Wisconsin writing session.

years.cap: Ratboys at Mutations Festival, Brighton, UK
years.src: Wikipedia: Singin' to an Empty Chair · Wikipedia: Ratboys
years.h: Singin' to an Empty Chair gets an 8.4 from Pitchfork
years.p: It's their sixth album and their first on New West, with Chris Walla producing again.
years.xp:
Ivy Nelson called it their most emotionally affecting and compositionally advanced songs to date. Stereogum's Tom Breihan wrote that it is "about as good as American indie rock gets." Metacritic lands at 85.

"Anywhere" was written around Sagan's dog's separation anxiety. "Burn It Down" was written during the 2020 George Floyd protests. Guests include Jenny Conlee, cellist Elizabeth Jordan and pedal steel player Andy Krull; Chris Shaw mixed and Heba Kadry mastered.

years.big: "Picture this: You're sitting across from a chair where no one else is sitting."
years.src: NPR: Ratboys · The Line of Best Fit · Wikipedia: Singin' to an Empty Chair
years.h: The title is a Gestalt therapy exercise
years.p: Steiner told NPR she used it to work through a fractured relationship with a loved one; the record ends on a Winnie the Pooh-inspired song.
years.xp: Steiner told NPR's World Cafe about the technique, in which you speak aloud to the empty seat as if the person were there. She told The Line of Best Fit the closing "At Peace in the Hundred Acre Woods" comes from the Pooh stories she read growing up and their friendship dynamics.

years.h: Three songs at the Tiny Desk, ending on an eight-minute centerpiece
years.p: "Penny in the Lake" and "What's Right?" come first, then "Black Earth, WI", for about 20 minutes in all.
years.xp: See Rock Live counts the set at three songs and about 20 minutes. LemonWire reports the Tiny Desk landed alongside a deluxe edition of the album with a Marked Men cover.
